chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: First dates with Sarah Vaughan in Baltimore and Chicago's Blue Note
summary: They resume as hang-out friends, playing Baltimore and a Chicago club that adores her.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But to go back to the Sarah Vaughan days, naturally, we were happy with each other, because we had worked together in the Eckstine band, and we'd always been good friends, and actually hang-out buddies when we were in the band. When I joined the trio, it was somewhat the same way. I played my

first engagement with her, I think it was in a club in Baltimore. Then we played a couple of places, and then we went to Chicago, and we played at a club there called the Blue Note, which was run by a guy, Frank... Oh boy! I mention him because he was a very fine guy, and he was crazy about Sarah Vaughan, and Sarah used to play there at least three or four times a year.
